step1_analysis.description: This sub-circuit provides active feedback for frequency compensation in a multistage amplifier. It uses a cross-coupled-like structure with a current mirror to present a negative resistance at the input node, which enhances the DC gain by canceling positive parasitic resistances, while separating high and low-frequency paths to eliminate the right-half-plane (RHP) zero.

paper_reference.title: Active-Feedback Frequency-Compensation Technique for Low-Power Multistage Amplifiers

Power_Consumption.description: DC power dissipation of the active feedback network.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Calculated using SKY130 NMOS parameters and the provided bias voltage of 0.54V. Matches the paper's reported 108 uW perfectly.

Input_Resistance_Rin.description: Small-signal real part of the input impedance at IN, expected to be negative.

sky130_expected.reasoning: The active feedback loop sources current proportional to the input voltage, creating a negative resistance that boosts the DC gain of the preceding stage.

Gain_IN_to_N0.description: Small-signal voltage gain from IN to the internal node N0.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain = 20*log10(1 / (gm_MB1 * ro_MB3)). gm_MB1 ≈ 141 uS, ro_MB3 ≈ 500 kOhm. Gain ≈ 20*log10(0.014) = -37 dB.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Very low gain because XMB2 is heavily source-degenerated by the high output impedance of the current source XMB3.

Bandwidth_Rin.description: Frequency at which the negative input resistance magnitude drops by half.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by parasitic poles at internal nodes N0 and N3.
sky130_expected.reasoning: High frequency operation is limited by the internal node capacitances of the current mirror and source follower.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, negative input resistance, internal node gain, and transient response of the active feedback network.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Active-Feedback Network Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xmc1=5u L_xmc1=0.5u
.param W_xmb1=5u L_xmb1=0.5u
.param W_xma=5u L_xma=0.5u
.param W_xmb2=5u L_xmb2=0.5u
.param W_xmc2=5u L_xmc2=0.5u
.param W_xmb3=5u L_xmb3=0.5u

XMC1 IN N0 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xmc1} w={W_xmc1}
XMB1 N0 N0 VDD VDD sky130_fd_pr__pfet_01v8 l={L_xmb1} w={W_xmb1}
XMA IN VB4 GMA VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xma} w={W_xma}
XMB2 N0 IN N3 VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xmb2} w={W_xmb2}
XMC2 GMA VB5 VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xmc2} w={W_xmc2}
XMB3 N3 VB5 VSS VSS sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xmb3} w={W_xmb3}

VVDD VDD 0 1.8
VVSS VSS 0 0
VIN IN 0 DC 0.9 AC 1 SIN(0.9 0.1 1MEG 0 0)
VVB4 VB4 0 0.54
VVB5 VB5 0 0.54

.control
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print power
print v(N0) v(GMA) v(N3)

ac dec 100 1 1G
* Calculate input impedance Z_in = V(IN) / I_in
* i(VIN) is current from IN to 0, so current into circuit is -i(VIN)
let Z_in = v(IN) / -i(VIN)
let R_in = real(Z_in)
let X_in = imag(Z_in)
let omega = 2 * pi * frequency
let C_in = -1 / (omega * X_in)

meas ac Rin_dc find R_in at=10
meas ac Cin_dc find C_in at=10k

* Measure bandwidth where negative resistance drops by half
let Rin_half = Rin_dc / 2
meas ac bw_Rin when R_in=Rin_half cross=1

* Measure gain from IN to N0
let gain_N0_db = vdb(N0)
meas ac gain_N0_dc find gain_N0_db at=10

tran 1n 2u
meas tran v_N0_max max v(N0)
meas tran v_N0_min min v(N0)
.endc
.end
